title: Everyday examples of zero net force
canonical_question: What are some everyday examples where the net force on an object is zero?
summary: A lamp on a desk, a picture on a wall and a parked car all have zero net force.
Zero net force also covers steady motion, like a car cruising at constant speed on a flat road.

reuse.rationale: Authored fixture node for the E05 registry.

sections.heading: Things sitting still
sections.body_md: A lamp on a desk, a picture on a wall and a parked car all have zero net force. In each case gravity is balanced by a support or friction. Nothing accelerates because the pushes and pulls cancel.

sections.heading: Things moving steadily
sections.body_md: Zero net force also covers steady motion, like a car cruising at constant speed on a flat road. There the engine’s drive force just balances drag and friction. Constant velocity, not only rest, signals zero net force.

key_points: Resting objects often have zero net force.
Steady motion also means zero net force.
Balance, not stillness, is the real test.
core.bridge_to_parent: It gives worked examples of the objective’s zero-net-force idea.

seeds: Can a moving object have zero net force?
